records.area: 100 Mile
records.headline: Special weather statement
records.description:
Fall Storm Bringing Mixed Weather Conditions today.

What:
- Sudden gusty winds of 60 to 80 km/h.
- Snow levels lowering to 1500 metres over southern B.C.
- Snow levels lowering to 1200 metres over central B.C.
- Risk of thunderstorms over Cariboo and Columbia regions.

When:
Today.

Where:
- Fraser Valley East including Hope
- Coquihalla Highway - Hope to Kamloops
- Highway 97C - Okanagan Connector
- Highway 3 - Hope to Princeton via Allison Pass
- Manning - Skagit Valley
- Similkameen
- Nicola
- 100 Mile
- Chilcotin
- Cariboo
- Prince George
- Stuart - Nechako
- Lakes District
-Yellowhead
-Yellowhead Highway - Tete Jaune Cache to the Alberta Border

Impacts:
- Possible localised utility outages
- Possible fallen branches
- High profile vehicles should take caution in high winds
- Possible slippery conditions over high elevation passes with wet snow

Additional information:
A sharp cold front moving across the B.C. Interior today will primarily generate strong gusty winds of 60 to 80 km/h. Snow levels will fall with the passage of this cold front and may produce some snow over high elevation highway passes. In the wake of the cold front, cold and unstable air will generate scattered showers, isolated thunderstorms with risk of small hail across the central interior and parts of the Columbia regions.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

Strong winds gusting to near 100 km/h are expected today.

These winds will diminish late this afternoon.

Local utility outages are possible. Driving conditions will likely be difficult. High-sided vehicles will be pushed around by the wind. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible.

Secure loose objects.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ABstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #ABStorm.

records.area: Broward, FL; Palm Beach, FL
records.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 17 at 4:44PM EDT until October 17 at 5:15PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
records.description:
At 444 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
3.5 and 5.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts
of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...

records.area: Ocracoke Island
records.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 17 at 3:46PM EDT until October 19 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
records.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, strong longshore
currents in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to 4
feet of inundation above ground level expected in low-lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf
Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 12 feet expected in the
surf zone.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 5 PM EDT
Tuesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from midnight tonight to
8 PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
expected in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of vehicles
will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be inundated,
especially around high tide. There is a possibility of being
stranded on Ocracoke for multiple days. This could be life
threatening if you have an emergency. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Strong longshore
currents will create dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This has the potential to be a long
duration event bringing more significant ocean overwash impacts
to vulnerable oceanside areas through multiple high tide cycles
into next week. Minor soundside water level rises will also be
possible.
records.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of unknown
depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property. Prepare for being stranded on Ocracoke for multiple
days. Prepare for disruptions to ferries by this evening and
lasting into at least part of next week.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

records.area: Rota
records.headline: Typhoon Warning issued October 18 at 4:40AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
records.description:
Updated for compact wind radii, reducing winds for Rota and Guam.

...TYPHOON CHAMPI NOW A DANGEROUS CATEGORY 4 MOVING WEST INTO GUAM
COASTAL WATERS...

.NEW INFORMATION...
None.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended actions for
people on Guam and on Rota, Tinian and Saipan in the Northern
Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
A Typhoon Warning continues for Guam and Rota.

A Tropical Storm Warning and a Typhoon Watch continues for Tinian
and Saipan.

A Flood Watch is in effect for Rota, Tinian and Saipan in the
Northern Marianas. Please listen closely for any Flood Warnings that
might be in effect for your area.

A Flash Flood Warning is now in effect for Guam.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 4 AM ChST...the center of Typhoon Champi (29W) was located near
latitude 13.1N...longitude 144.9E. This was about 25 miles southeast
of Guam. Storm motion was west, 280 degrees, at 15 mph. Storm
intensity was 140 mph. This general forecast track will take Champi
about 15 miles south of Guam as a Category 4 typhoon as it intensifies
further the next few days west of the Marianas.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Typhoon Champi (29W) has been undergoing rapid intensification
today. As a result it is now a dangerous category 4 typhoon. It is
expected to pass a little south of Guam as a super typhoon within
the next 12 hours. This may potentially bring devastating wind
conditions to much of Guam during passage.

.PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...
records.instruction:
Tropical storm conditions will soon occur. Get to safe shelter now if
you are not already there. Everyone should remain alert and stay
inside.

Listen for possible flood warnings.

records.description:

...TYPHOON CHAMPI NOW A DANGEROUS CATEGORY 4 MOVING WEST INTO GUAM
COASTAL WATERS...

.NEW INFORMATION...
None.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended actions for
people on Guam and on Rota, Tinian and Saipan in the Northern
Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
A Typhoon Warning continues for Guam and Rota.

A Tropical Storm Warning and a Typhoon Watch continues for Tinian
and Saipan.

A Flood Watch is in effect for Rota, Tinian and Saipan in the
Northern Marianas. Please listen closely for any Flood Warnings that
might be in effect for your area.

A Flash Flood Warning is now in effect for Guam.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 4 AM ChST...the center of Typhoon Champi (29W) was located near
latitude 13.1N...longitude 144.9E. This was about 25 miles southeast
of Guam. Storm motion was west, 280 degrees, at 15 mph. Storm
intensity was 140 mph. This general forecast track will take Champi
about 15 miles south of Guam as a Category 4 typhoon as it intensifies
further the next few days west of the Marianas.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Typhoon Champi (29W) has been undergoing rapid intensification
today. As a result it is now a dangerous category 4 typhoon. It is
expected to pass a little south of Guam as a super typhoon within
the next 12 hours. This may potentially bring devastating wind
conditions to much of Guam during passage.

.PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...
records.instruction:
Dangerous typhoon conditions will soon occur for central and southern
Guam. Everyone should be quickly moving to safety within their home
or shelter. Once inside, ensure all windows and doors are secured
before dangerous winds arrive. Move to an interior room on the lowest
floor.

Be aware that the loss of commercial power can happen quickly.
Keep emergency gear handy.

records.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 17 at 1:23PM CDT until October 17 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
records.description:
...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS POSSIBLE TODAY...

.Conditions will remain favorable for the spread of fires through
the remainder of this afternoon due to the combination of dry
fuels, low humidity, strong winds.

* AFFECTED AREA...Pointe Coupee, West Feliciana, East Feliciana,
St. Helena, Washington, Iberville, West Baton Rouge, East
Baton Rouge, Assumption, St. James, Wilkinson, Amite, Pike,
Northern Tangipahoa, Walthall, Southeast St. Tammany, Pearl
River, Northern St. Tammany, Southwestern St. Tammany,
Hancock, Central Tangipahoa, Harrison, Lower Tangipahoa,
Jackson, Northern Livingston, Southern Livingston, Western
Ascension and Eastern Ascension.

* WINDS...North 15 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 32 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
records.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

records.area: Guam; Rota
records.headline: Flood Watch issued October 18 at 4:12AM ChST until October 18 at 6:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
records.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Guam, Rota.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains
and ditches may become clogged with debris. Extensive street
flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Typhoon Champi (29W) will produce locally heavy rainfall late
tonight and Sunday, though expected rainfall has decreased
slightly as the larger rainbands remain mainly south and east of
the center of Champi. Rota could receive 3 to 5 inches, and Guam
might get 4 to 8 inches.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
records.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

records.area: Aransas Islands; Kleberg Islands; Nueces Islands; Calhoun Islands
records.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 17 at 1:09PM CDT until October 18 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
records.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Aransas Islands, Kleberg Islands, Nueces Islands and
Calhoun Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 AM CDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, until 7 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the most experienced swimmers away from shore into deeper
water. These rip currents can become life-threatening to
anyone entering the surf.
records.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

records.area: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
records.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 17 at 12:55PM CDT until October 18 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
records.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 10
feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 AM CDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
records.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

records.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 17 at 9:11AM PDT until October 17 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
records.description:
...RISK FOR RAPID FIRE GROWTH AND EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH ANY
NEW FIRE STARTS TODAY, DUE TO GUSTY SANTA ANA WINDS WITH VERY WARM
AND DRY CONDITIONS...

Offshore winds are not as strong or widespread as the past couple
of days, but will still create a risk for new fires to have rapid
growth in wind prone areas of LA/Ventura counties due to the very
warm and dry conditions. By this afternoon, offshore winds may
weaken sufficiently to allow some Red Flag Warning areas to be
cancelled early.

* AFFECTED AREA...Santa Clarita Valley, Ventura County Beaches,
Ventura County Inland Coast, Lake Casitas, Ojai Valley,
Central Ventura County Valleys, Malibu Coast, Calabasas and
Agoura Hills, Western San Fernando Valley, Eastern San
Fernando Valley, Southeastern Ventura County Valleys and Los
Angeles County San Gabriel Valley.

* TIMING...Until 8 PM PDT this evening.

* WINDS...Northeast to east 15 to 25 mph with gusts of 30 to 40
mph, gradually diminishing in the afternoon. Strongest winds
in Ventura county and eastern San Gabriel Valley foothills.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 10 to 20 percent common.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable
for extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and
property.
records.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

records.area: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
records.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 17 at 9:31AM EDT until October 20 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
records.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 10
feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Monday
night. For the High Surf Advisory, from 11 PM this evening to
4 AM EDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
records.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

records.area: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
records.headline: Flood Warning issued October 17 at 9:04AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
records.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to remain in Minor Flood
Stage today, then strong northeasterly winds will slow river flow
leading to a quick rise in levels. The river is forecast to reach
Moderate Flood Stage late Sunday to early Monday, with a steady
increase through Moderate Flood Stage forecast next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.3 feet, Many docks become submerged along the river
and in canals in the Astor community. Water enters yards of
properties on Bartram Road, Holiday Circle and along Wild Hog Road
on the Lake County side. In Volusia County, water encroaches yards
of homes on the river side of Alice Drive. No wake zones are in
effect from near the South Moon Canal to approximately 800 feet
south of the Riverview lodge. At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps
covered at South Moon Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's
Jungle Den. Water approaching sites closest to the river at Fish
Tales RV Resort and Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair
Street covered by river water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks
underwater at the Astor Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive.
Portions of Fox Road are covered with water nearest to the river.
Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud roads are underwater with yards
inundated. At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane. At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed
into yards. Homes on or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become
inaccessible with several inches of water inside homes along the
river and canals. Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor
are completely submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are
inaccessible with yards completely submerged. Clair Street is
inaccessible. Roads flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and
yards at condominiums on Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall
at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 2.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Saturday was 2.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.3 feet early next
week following a period of persistent northeasterly winds.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
records.instruction:

through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

records.area: Tinian Coastal Waters; Saipan Coastal Waters
records.headline: Typhoon Watch issued October 17 at 10:39PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
records.description:
* WHAT...Tropical storm conditions, including winds of 34 to 63 knots,
are expected. Typhoon conditions, including winds of 64 knots or
more are possible.

* WHERE...Tinian and Saipan Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Onset of damaging winds beginning late tonight, continuing
into at least Sunday night, possibly longer if conditions warrant.

* IMPACTS...Destructive winds will produce dangerous seas that could
damage, capsize or sink vessels, along with drastically reducing
visibilities in heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Typhoon Champi (29W) continues to move quickly
toward the Marianas. The exact path of 29W remains subject to
change. However, guidance supports a passage through Guam coastal
waters, a bit south of Guam, with damaging winds moving into Tinian
and Saipan Waters tonight and lasting into at least Sunday evening.
Champi is expected to strengthen further as it approaches, then move
through the region as a category 4 super typhoon Sunday morning.
Seas are quickly rising, with significant sea heights reaching as
high as 25 feet during closest passage of Champi. Dangerous sea
conditions may continue into Monday.
records.instruction:
Prepare for tropical storm
force conditions through Sunday night. Secure all vessels. Conditions
are expected to be extremely dangerous for small craft, and dangerous
for any vessels of larger size. As Typhoon Champi approaches the
Marianas, stay in safe harbor.

records.area: Guam Coastal Waters; Rota Coastal Waters
records.headline: Typhoon Warning issued October 17 at 10:39PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
records.description:
* WHAT...Typhoon conditions, including winds of 64 knots or more
are expected.

* WHERE...Guam and Rota Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Damaging winds are occurring in eastern waters, and will
begin later tonight in western waters. Onset of destructive winds
after midnight with typhoon force winds early Sunday morning.
Damaging winds will continue into at least Sunday night, especially
if Champi slows down.

* IMPACTS...Destructive to typhoon force winds will produce
dangerous to deadly seas that could damage, capsize or sink
vessels, along with drastically reducing visibilities in heavy
rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Typhoon Champi (29W) continues to move quickly
toward the Marianas. The exact path of 29W remains subject to
change. However, guidance supports a passage through Guam coastal
waters, a little south of Guam, with damaging winds moving in late
tonight and lasting into at least Sunday night. Champi is expected
to strengthen further as it approaches, then move through the
region as a category 4 super typhoon Sunday morning. Seas are
quickly rising, with significant sea heights reaching as high as
35 feet near the eye wall of Champi. Dangerous sea conditions may
continue into Monday.
records.instruction:
Prepare for the passage of a
category 4 typhoon Sunday morning. Secure all vessels. Conditions are
expected to be catastrophic for small craft, and extremely dangerous
for any vessels of larger size. As Typhoon Champi approaches, stay
in safe harbor.

records.area: Inland Chatham; Coastal Chatham; Beaufort; Coastal Colleton; Charleston; Coastal Jasper; Tidal Berkeley
records.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 17 at 4:53AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
records.description:
Gusty north winds will impact the region today in the wake of a
strong cold front. Winds on some of the taller bridges and elevated
roadways around the Charleston, Beaufort and Savannah Metro Areas and
nearby barrier islands, could see gusts as high as 40 mph at times
making for hazardous driving conditions.

Some of these bridges include the Ravenel Bridge, the Don Holt
Bridge, the James B. Edwards Bridge, the Ben Sawyer Bridge, the Isle
of Palms connector, the James Island Connector, the Amos Nathaniel
Rodgers Bridge, the McKinley Washington Junior Bridge, the Woods
Memorial Bridge, the Edward Burton Rodgers Bridge, the Harbor River
Bridge and the Talmadge Memorial Bridge.

Vehicles driving on these bridges should use extra caution,
particularly high profile vehicles.
records.instruction:
Stay tuned to NOAA Weather Radio All Hazards, TV or your local news
source for the latest information from the National Weather Service.

records.area: Coastal waters from Cape Blanco OR to Pt. St. George CA out 10 nm
records.headline: Hazardous Seas Warning issued October 17 at 1:03AM PDT until October 18 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Medford OR
records.description:
* WHAT...For the Hazardous Seas Warning, north winds 20 to 30 kt
with gusts to 35 kt and very steep and hazardous seas 8 to 12
ft due to a mix of wind seas and building swell at 11 seconds
expected. For the Small Craft Advisory, north winds 15 to 25
kt with gusts up to 30 kt and steep seas 7 to 9 ft due to a
mix of wind seas and building swell at 11 seconds expected.

* WHERE...Small craft advisory conditions will affect all the
area Saturday afternoon. Then, late Saturday afternoon through
early Sunday morning, Hazardous Seas Warning conditions will
affect areas south of Port Orford beyond 5 nm from shore with
Small Craft Advisory elsewhere. Small craft advisory seas will
return Sunday morning and afternoon.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, from 11 AM this morning
to 5 PM PDT Sunday. For the Hazardous Seas Warning, from 5 PM
this afternoon to 5 AM PDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Very steep and hazardous seas could capsize or
damage vessels. Bar crossings will become especially
treacherous.

* View the hazard area in detail at https://go.usa.gov/x6hks
records.instruction:
Recreational boaters should remain in port. Commercial vessels
should prepare for very steep seas and consider remaining in port
until conditions improve.

records.area: Lincoln; Union; Jackson; Ouachita; Natchitoches; Winn; Grant; Caldwell; La Salle
records.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 17 at 2:51AM CDT until October 17 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA
records.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 9 AM THIS MORNING TO 7 PM
CDT THIS EVENING DUE TO WIND SHIFT, MOISTURE DROP AND WIND, LOW
RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR PORTIONS OF NORTH CENTRAL AND NORTHWEST
LOUISIANA...

* AFFECTED AREA...Portions of north central and northwest Louisiana.

* TIMING...From 9 AM this morning to 7 PM CDT this evening.

* WINDS...Northeast winds 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 31 to 69 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
records.instruction:
Please advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the field of
this Red Flag Warning.

Follow all fire restrictions. One less spark, one less wildfire.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions that
promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This
does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.

records.area: Orange County Coastal; Orange County Inland
records.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 16 at 6:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
records.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
increased fine particle pollution from wildfire smoke.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in the areas of San Clemente, Dana Point, San Juan
Capistrano, and Laguna Niguel. Levels of particle pollution can
vary by time and location depending on fire activity and local
weather conditions.

* WHEN...from 4 PM Friday to 10 AM Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Particles in wildfire smoke can get deep into the lungs
and cause serious health problems such as heart attacks, strokes,
asthma attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected,
but people with lung or heart disease, older adults, people who are
pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot of time outdoors are
at greater risk.
records.instruction:
To protect your health, if you smell or see smoke:

* Remain indoors with windows and doors closed
* Avoid intense outdoor physical activity
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* If you must be outdoors, keep the time brief and wear a well-
fitting N-95 mask
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

For the latest air quality forecasts and information, visit the
website at aqmd.gov.

records.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 16 at 6:02PM CDT until October 17 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
records.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING FOR PORTIONS OF SOUTHEAST TEXAS AND CENTRAL
AND SOUTHWEST LOUISIANA FRIDAY AND SATURDAY...

.Breezy and dry conditions due to a frontal passage will combine
with very dry fuels resulting in a period of high fire danger.
Red flag conditions will develop across portions of central and
southwest Louisiana and southeast Texas Friday afternoon and
evening, before winds decrease and humidity recovers some
overnight. Red flag conditions will then be expected again across
all of central and southwest Louisiana and southeast Texas during
the day Saturday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 031 Allen, Fire Weather Zone
032 Evangeline, Fire Weather Zone 033 St. Landry, Fire Weather
Zone 044 Lafayette, Fire Weather Zone 045 Upper St. Martin,
Fire Weather Zone 055 Lower St. Martin, Fire Weather Zone 073
West Cameron, Fire Weather Zone 074 East Cameron, Fire Weather
Zone 141 Northern Calcasieu, Fire Weather Zone 142 Northern
Jefferson Davis, Fire Weather Zone 143 Northern Acadia, Fire
Weather Zone 152 Upper Vermilion, Fire Weather Zone 153 Upper
Iberia, Fire Weather Zone 154 Upper St. Mary, Fire Weather
Zone 201 Hardin, Fire Weather Zone 241 Southern Calcasieu,
Fire Weather Zone 242 Southern Jefferson Davis, Fire Weather
Zone 243 Southern Acadia, Fire Weather Zone 252 Lower
Vermilion, Fire Weather Zone 253 Lower Iberia, Fire Weather
Zone 254 Lower St. Mary, Fire Weather Zone 261 Southern
Jasper, Fire Weather Zone 262 Southern Newton, Fire Weather
Zone 515 Upper Jefferson, Fire Weather Zone 516 Northern
Orange, Fire Weather Zone 615 Lower Jefferson and Fire Weather
Zone 616 Southern Orange.

* TIMING...From 9 AM to 8 PM CDT Saturday.

* WINDS...North 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 31 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Up to 73.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
records.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.
